title: Slicing: an lfp immersion cutting the source fibre dimension by one when the stabilizer is smaller

proof_spans.label: the author's own proof environment immediately following the lemma: Over affine neighbourhoods with u a closed point, the local ring of the scheme-theoretic source fibre at e(u) is Cohen-Macaulay of dimension d_2 by hypothesis. Restricting the groupoid to the point u identifies the local ring of the restricted arrow scheme with the fibre ring modulo both s(m) and t(m), and the chain of restriction and stabilizer dimension lemmas evaluates its dimension as d_1. Since d_1 is smaller, prime avoidance over the finitely many minimal primes of the Cohen-Macaulay fibre ring produces an element f of the maximal ideal whose t-image avoids them all, and the one-equation lemma cuts the fibre dimension below d_2. The quotient A/fA gives the immersion U', non-zerodivisibility of t(f) on the Cohen-Macaulay fibre ring together with the Grothendieck flatness criterion makes h Cohen-Macaulay at (u, e(u)), and the dimension of the cut fibre is d_2 minus one exactly. (source lines 2094-2236)

core_obligations: Choose an affine neighbourhood Spec(A) of u with u closed (02J2) and an affine neighbourhood Spec(B) of e(u) mapping into the product of squares; the induced maps on residue fields agree and are isomorphisms since e is a simultaneous section of s and t, so the prime q over e(u) is maximal; the local ring of the fibre F_u at e(u) is B_q modulo s(m)B_q, Cohen-Macaulay of dimension d_2 by hypothesis and 02FX (proof lines 2094-2129). Restrict the groupoid to the point u: the restriction lemmas give a groupoid scheme with locally finite type maps (lemma-restrict-preserves-type), dim of the restricted arrow scheme equals dim of its stabilizer (lemma-groupoid-on-field-dimension-equal-stabilizer) and equals the dimension of its local ring at the identity (lemma-groupoid-on-field-locally-finite-type-dimension), while the stabilizer of the restriction is the fibre G_u of the stabilizer (groupoids-lemma-restrict-stabilizer, tag 04ML); hence the local ring of R'' at e'' has dimension d_1 (proof lines 2131-2146). Compute R'' as the base change of R over the product of residue fields: its local ring at e'' is B_q modulo s(m)B_q and t(m)B_q, of dimension d_1 (proof lines 2148-2168). Claim: some f in m cuts the dimension below d_2 (proof lines 2170-2197): the minimal primes n_j of the Cohen-Macaulay fibre ring are finite in number, each has quotient of dimension d_2 (algebra-lemma-CM-dim-formula, tag 00NA), the further quotient by t(m)B_q has dimension at most d_1 as a quotient of the computed local ring, so the maximal ideal is not inside any t-preimage of n_j, and prime avoidance (algebra-lemma-silly, tag 00DS) yields f in m with t(f) outside all n_j; the inequality follows from algebra-lemma-one-equation (tag 00KW). Set A' = A/fA: U' is an immersed closed subscheme of the affine neighbourhood, locally of finite presentation, containing u, giving (1), (2), (3) (proof lines 2200-2202). The map h corresponds to the ring map A to B modulo t(f)B; t(f) is a non-zerodivisor on the positive-dimensional Cohen-Macaulay fibre ring since it lies in no minimal prime (algebra-lemma-reformulate-CM, tag 02JN), so by the Grothendieck criterion (algebra-lemma-grothendieck-general, tag 046Z) the local map is flat with Cohen-Macaulay fibre ring, giving (4) (proof lines 2203-2225). By the restriction diagram (equation-restriction) the fibre F'_u is the fibre of h over u, so its dimension at e'(u) is the dimension of the cut fibre ring, which is d_2 minus one by 02JN once more, giving (5) (proof lines 2226-2235).
proof_roadmap: Set up affine neighbourhoods and identify the Cohen-Macaulay fibre ring of dimension d_2 (proof lines 2094-2129).

Compute the local ring of the restricted arrow scheme at the identity as the fibre ring modulo s(m) and t(m) and evaluate its dimension as d_1 through the restriction and stabilizer lemmas (proof lines 2131-2168).
Choose f by minimal primes and prime avoidance so that the cut fibre dimension drops below d_2 (proof lines 2170-2197).
The quotient A/fA gives the immersion with (1), (2), (3); non-zerodivisibility plus the Grothendieck criterion give flatness with Cohen-Macaulay fibre, i.e. (4) (proof lines 2200-2225).
Identify F'_u with the fibre of h and read off dimension d_2 minus one for (5) (proof lines 2226-2235).
